card.name: Word starts before patient-group phrases
card.fires_on: Fires on a small word like "in" or "patients" right before a patient group ("in these patients", "in patients with"). Also on a hyphen-plus-letter piece like "-b" in "sponge-bathe" and "statin-benefiting".

modes.label: In before patients
modes.description: The word "in" at the start of a sentence or phrase, leading into "these patients" or "patients with".
modes.example: perfusion.<< In>> these patients, administration of an NSAID

modes.label: Hyphen-b word pieces
modes.description: The "-b" piece after a noun or verb that begins a compound such as bathe or benefiting.
modes.example: You may need to sponge<<-b>>athe until your doctor says you may shower

modes.label: Start of a drug name
modes.description: The opening piece of a drug name in a list of drugs.

card.writes: It seems to push toward words like officers, priesthood and people groups, and away from health and healthcare words.
card.plain: It fires on small words that lead into a group of patients, and on the start of some split words.
